note: Officeholders and districts as listed by NH RSA 662 (districts), Citizens Count, the NH General Court, the NH Executive Council, Ballotpedia, the Conway Daily Sun, Carroll County and The Ballot Brief, checked Oct 30, 2026. North Conway is a village in the Town of Conway, so every district below is the Town of Conway's. Positions are the officials' own survey answers or quoted statements, with the year. Nothing here is characterized or scored.
ballot_note: Governor, U.S. Senate, U.S. House (NH-1), Executive Council District 1, State Senate District 3, Conway's three State House seats (Carroll 1), County Commissioner District 1 and the county sheriff, attorney, treasurer, register of deeds and register of probate are all on the Tuesday, Nov 3, 2026 ballot. Conway votes at the Town Garage, 1611 East Main St., Center Conway, 8am to 7pm. Results will replace the names below.

levels.title: Federal
levels.blurb: Two senators and one representative. All of Carroll County, including Conway, is in New Hampshire's 1st Congressional District.

levels.title: State
levels.blurb: The Governor, your Executive Councilor (Conway is in District 1) and your State Senator (Conway is in District 3).

levels.title: State House
levels.blurb: Conway is its own three-seat district, Carroll 1, and no floterial district includes Conway (RSA 662:5). All three seats are on the Nov 3 ballot; two of the three current members are not running for them.

levels.title: Carroll County
levels.blurb: The three county commissioners are the county's executive board, in charge of the county budget, nursing home, jail and staff; the sheriff, county attorney, treasurer and registries also sit under the county. Conway is in Commissioner District 1 with Albany, Bartlett, Chatham, Hart's Location, Jackson, Sandwich and Hale's Location. Every county office is on the Nov 3 ballot.

kenney.name: Joseph D. Kenney
kenney.status: The five-member Executive Council approves state contracts, confirms judges and commissioners, and reviews pardon requests. Conway is in District 1. Also served on the Council 2014 to 2019 and in the NH House and Senate before that. Two-year term, on the Nov 3 ballot with Luz Bay (D).
positions: "I will oppose and vote against any and all efforts to increase taxes."
"All contracts should be put out to bid. It's the American way!"
Against state push on local zoning
"No, New Hampshire prides itself on local control. Town Fathers and Mothers need to make their own decisions"
"I would be more interested in their constitutional beliefs, legal experiences, professional recommendations, and community service."
"New Hampshire needs to enforce what is currently on the books for gun laws."
kenney.caveat: Citizens Count shows "No Response" for his 2026 Citizens Count survey questions; the 2026 answer is from the Granite State Taxpayers survey.

mcconkey.name: Mark E. McConkey
mcconkey.status: District 3 covers Conway and most of Carroll County plus several Grafton and Strafford towns. Of Freedom. Served in the NH House 2002 to 2018 and 2020 to 2024. Two-year term, on the Nov 3 ballot with Bobbi Boudman (D).
positions: "my priorities have always been to protect New Hampshire's values of strong communities, low taxes and personal freedom."
"Our state roads and bridges are crucial for local businesses, tourism and keeping our families safe."
"Whether it is protecting the shorelines and dams on our lakes, or improving safety on Route 16."
mcconkey.caveat: His Citizens Count profile could not be opened in this session; these quotes are from his May 2024 Senate campaign announcement as published by InDepthNH. Service years and contact details are from his NH Senate page (gc.nh.gov/Senate/members/webpages/district03.aspx).

buco.name: Thomas "Tom" Buco
buco.status: Carroll 1 is the town of Conway alone and elects three representatives; no floterial district includes Conway. In this district since Dec 2022; his House page says he has served ten terms. Not on the Nov 3 ballot.

paige.name: David Paige
paige.status: Carroll 1 is the town of Conway alone and elects three representatives. Member of the House Housing Committee. Two-year term, on the Nov 3 ballot for reelection.

Against relying mainly on property taxes

woodcock.name: Stephen Woodcock
woodcock.status: Carroll 1 is the town of Conway alone and elects three representatives. Not on the Nov 3 ballot for this seat. A Democrat listed as Steve (The Ballot Brief) or Stephen (GoodParty.org) Woodcock is the Democratic candidate for Carroll County Register of Probate; not confirmed that this is the same person.

chandler.name: Gene G. Chandler
chandler.status: Of Bartlett. District 1 is Albany, Bartlett, Chatham, Conway, Hart's Location, Jackson, Sandwich and Hale's Location. A former NH House speaker, appointed by the county delegation in May 2025 after Terry McCarthy (R-Conway) resigned, to serve until the Nov 2026 election. On the Nov 3 ballot with Wharton Sinkler (D).

statusSrc.label: The Ballot Brief, Carroll County Commissioner District 1

positions: "I don't have any agenda at all, and I'm open for listening to whatever goes on and making the best decisions I can"

mcgee.name: Charles "Chuck" McGee
mcgee.status: Of Moultonborough; board chair as of May 2025. Appointed in 2023 to fill a vacancy and won the Nov 2024 election. District 2 (Madison, Moultonborough, Ossipee, Tamworth, Tuftonboro) does not include Conway. On the Nov 3 ballot with Tom Randell (D); Conway voters do not vote in this race.

parker.name: Harold B. Parker
parker.status: Of Wolfeboro. District 3 (Brookfield, Eaton, Effingham, Freedom, Wakefield, Wolfeboro) does not include Conway. On the Nov 3 ballot with Michael Parton (D); Conway voters do not vote in this race.
parker.caveat: First year in office not confirmed from an opened source.

richardi.name: Domenic M. Richardi
richardi.status: Of Conway. Won every general election for sheriff from 2012 through 2024, usually on both party lines. Won the Sep 8, 2026 Republican primary over Justin Worthley and is the only candidate on Nov 3.

blair.name: Keith D. Blair
blair.status: Of Wolfeboro. The county's chief prosecutor. Deputy county attorney from 2021; the only applicant to succeed Michaela Andruzzi in Oct 2023, then elected in 2024. The only filer for county attorney on Nov 3.

sawyer.name: Matt Sawyer, Jr.
sawyer.status: Took office Jan 2025, replacing the late Joe Costello. Won the Sep 8 Republican primary over Andrea Piccard; the only candidate on Nov 3.

statusSrc.label: The Ballot Brief, Carroll County Treasurer

rines.name: Karen I. Rines
rines.status: Of Ossipee. Took office Jan 2025, replacing Lisa Scott. The only filer for register of deeds on Nov 3.
